question: What is the scientific name of green pea?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pisum sativum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The scientific name **"Pisum sativum"** is used to classify the green pea, which belongs to the family **Fabaceae (legumes).**
 
• Green peas are widely consumed as a vegetable and are known for their **nutritional benefits**, including being a good source of vitamins, minerals, and protein.
 
• Pisum sativum is cultivated in** temperate regions** around the world and is typically planted in the spring.
 
• There are several varieties of Pisum sativum, including **garden peas, snap peas, and snow peas**, each with different uses in cooking and food preparation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zea mays (Corn/Maize):**

 
 
• Zea mays is a cereal grain **first domesticated** by indigenous peoples in **southern Mexico** about 10,000 years ago.
 
• The **United States is the largest producer **of maize, followed by **China and Brazil.**
 
 
 
• **Triticum aestivum (Common Wheat):**
 
 
• Triticum aestivum is **one of the most widely cultivated **species of wheat and is a key staple food worldwide.
 
• Wheat is grown in diverse climates and is a major crop in countries like **China, India, and the United States.**
 
 
 
• **Pisum sativum (Green Pea):**
 
 
• Green peas help **improve soil fertility** through nitrogen fixation, benefiting subsequent crops in rotation.
 
• The main types include garden peas, which are typically consumed **fresh; snow peas, which have edible pods; and snap peas**, which are sweet and crunchy.
